problem.text: Ordinary MLP projections implicitly used Linear's 128-element alignment. Because both projections disallow input padding, hidden and intermediate widths not divisible by 128 could fail construction.

reasoning.text: The change exposes pad_to on MLP and forwards it to both projections. Setting pad_to=1 preserves the requested dimensions without removing Linear's input-padding assertion; the default 128 preserves prior behavior.

impact.text: This enables callers to construct unpadded ordinary MLPs, rather than changing GatedMLP or automatically selecting unpadded storage for existing models. The whole-parent-tree MLP search found no ordinary MLP construction sites or subclasses.

source_notes.text: The initial modules entry was read. It establishes the original distinction between ordinary down(silu(up(x))) computation and GatedMLP's selectable activation.

Issue #38, “Error converting nvidia/Llama-3_1-Nemotron-Ultra-253B-v1,” reports sliced GatedMLP loading failure. Issues #34, “torch._C._LinAlgError on last layer of quant,” and #42, “converting to 3.0 bpw causes error; block state has 0 inf values and 34 NaN values,” report quantization failures. Their connection here is inferred only from shared mlp.py/linear.py paths; none establishes that this ordinary-MLP change fixes those reports.

limitations: No model, tensor loader, PyTorch operation or GPU kernel was executed. The scalar check establishes dimension arithmetic only, not arbitrary-width FP16 or EXL3 runtime compatibility.
The repository search establishes no ordinary MLP constructor callers; dynamic or external callers remain outside that evidence.

claims.text: pad_to is an alignment multiple, not a dtype selector. Linear rounds each dimension with ceil(width/pad_to)*pad_to. Passing the same alignment to up and down keeps their intermediate dimensions consistent; using 1 leaves both hidden and intermediate widths exact.

For ordinary weights, Linear.load_fp16 passes the resolved dimensions as loader padding targets and constructs LinearFP16 with them. LinearFP16.forward preserves leading dimensions and uses its out_features for the output width, selecting torch.matmul when input and output dtypes agree and ext.hgemm otherwise. The patch changes dimension preparation, not that execution dispatch.

A standard-library transcription checked widths 130 and 257: alignment 128 produces 256 and 384 and fails both input-equality conditions; alignment 1 preserves 130 and 257 and satisfies them. It also checked identity for widths 1 through 1024 at alignment 1.
MLP.forward remains up → SiLU → down with its existing output-dtype conversion. The newly accepted activation_fn argument is not stored or consumed, unlike GatedMLP's existing activation selector.

findings.description: The added activation_fn parameter silently has no effect.
findings.trigger: An external caller constructs an otherwise valid MLP with activation_fn="gelu" and then calls forward.
findings.expected_behavior: Honor the requested activation or explicitly reject unsupported selections.
findings.actual_behavior: The constructor ignores activation_fn and forward unconditionally applies F.silu. No in-tree ordinary MLP constructor caller was found, so demonstrated reach is the exposed API rather than an existing model workflow.

verification.description: Compared the complete patch with the parent constructor and forward method; searched the whole parent tree for MLP references and inspected transformer consumers.
verification.limits: No runtime activation comparison or external caller inspection.

annotation.summary: Exposes ordinary MLP projection alignment so pad_to=1 preserves unpadded dimensions, retaining the default 128 alignment. Also adds an activation_fn argument that remains unused.

argv:
for p in (128,1):
 h,i=130,257
 ph=(h+p-1)//p*p; pi=(i+p-1)//p*p
 print({'pad_to':p,'up_shape':(ph,pi),'down_shape':(pi,ph),'up_input_assert':h==ph,'down_input_assert':i==pi})
assert all((n+1-1)//1*1==n for n in range(1,1025))
print('pad_to=1 preserves all widths 1..1024')
